## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to craft robust, portable one-liners using find and shell loops. The solution must exclude volatile filesystems (/proc and /sys), resolve symbolic link targets with readlink -f, and gracefully handle unreadable files while providing a reliable inventory of broken links across large directory trees.

## Key Concepts

- Find with -print0 and path pruning for safe filename handling
- readlink -f for canonical target resolution
- Robust error handling for unreadable targets and filesystem boundaries

## Code Example

```bash
find / -path /proc -prune -o -path /sys -prune -o -type l -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' l; do t=$(readlink -f "$l" 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$t" ] && [ ! -e "$t" ]; then echo "$l -> $t"; fi; done
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to integrate text and JSON logs, handle rotation and compression, and produce actionable, concise output under time pressure. 

## Key Concepts
- Normalizing heterogeneous log formats
- Safe traversal of rotated and gzipped files
- Shell pipelines, associative counting, and sorting for top results

## Code Example
```bash
find /logs/cluster -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.log.gz' \) -newermt '-6 hours' -print0 | \
  xargs -0 -I{} sh -c 'case {} in *.gz) zcat {} ;; *) cat {} ;; esac' | \
  awk 'BEGIN{IGNORECASE=1} /ERROR/ { if(match($0,/"msg":"([^"]+)"/,m)) msg=m[1]; else { if(match($0,/ERROR/)){ msg=$0 } } if(msg) c[msg]++ } END{for(k in c) print c[k],"|",k}' | \
  sort -nr | head -n5
```

- How would you adapt this to deduplicate identical messages across multiple hosts? 
- How would you verify correctness when logs are partially missing or severely skewed in time coverage?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to craft a robust shell one-liner using fundamental Unix tools for real-world security policy audits. It handles spaces in paths correctly, ignores unreadable files, and explicitly skips `.git` and `.svn` directories.

## Key Concepts
- **`-name .git -o -name .svn -prune`**: Skips `.git` and `.svn` directories entirely using find's prune action
- **`-perm -002`**: Matches files with world-writable permissions (any write bit set for "others")
- **`-not -user root`**: Excludes files owned by root
- **`-mtime -7`**: Selects files modified within the last 7 days
- **`%h` in `-printf`**: Prints the directory path (head) containing each matching file
- **Aggregation**: `sort | uniq -c` counts occurrences per unique directory, then `awk` formats the output as `directory:count`

## Code Example
```bash
find /shared \( -name .git -o -name .svn \) -prune -o -type f -perm -002 -not -user root -mtime -7 -printf '%h\n' | sort | uniq -c | awk '{printf "%s:%d\n", $2, $1}'
```

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to reason about stale PIDs, unreadable files, and craft robust one-liners with standard UNIX tools. Demonstrates safe parsing, process existence checks, and resilient file handling.

## Key Concepts

- POSIX shell loops and pipelines
- /proc existence checks
- Safe PID extraction
- Handling unreadable files

## Code Example

```bash
find /var/run -name '*.pid' -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | \
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do \
    pid=$(head -n1 "$f" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]'); \
    if [ -n "$pid" ] && [ ! -d "/proc/$pid" ]; then \
      svc=$(basename "$f" .pid); \
      printf "%s %s %s\n" "$svc" "$pid" "$(stat -c '%y' "$f" 2>/dev/null)"; \
    fi; \
  done | sort
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this for systems using journald or an alternative pid storage?
- How would you monitor this script output over time and alert on a rising stale PID count?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests real-world Unix skills: multi-format log parsing, compressed file handling, time-window filtering, and robust deduplication amid log rotation. It also probes fault tolerance with unreadable files and timezone quirks.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-format parsing (text and JSON)
- Handling multi-line blocks
- Reading compressed logs without external tools
- Time-window calculations with varying timezones
- Per-host deduplication across rotated logs

## Code Example
```bash
find /logs -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.log.gz' \) -print0 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r -d'' f; do
  host=$(hostname)
  if [[ "$f" == *.gz ]]; then
    zcat "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
  else
    cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
  fi
done | awk -v cutoff=$(date -d '8 hours ago' +%s) '
  # Parse text format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS LEVEL: text
  /^[[:digit:]]{4}-[[:digit:]]{2}-[[:digit:]]{2} / {
    split($1, d, "-")
    split($2, t, ":")
    ts = mktime(sprintf("%s %s %s %s %s %s", d[1], d[2], d[3], t[1], t[2], t[3]))
    if (ts >= cutoff && $4 ~ /ERROR/) {
      msg = substr($0, index($0, $4) + length($4) + 2)
      gsub(/[^a-z0-9]/, "", tolower(msg))
      print "ERROR:" host "|" msg
    }
    next
  }
  # Parse JSON format: {"ts":"...","lvl":"ERROR","msg":"..."}
  /^{.*"lvl".*:.*"ERROR"/ {
    match($0, /"ts": *"([^"]+)"/, m)
    match($0, /"msg": *"([^"]+)"/, m2)
    if (m[1] && m2[1]) {
      split(m[1], dt, /[T:+-]/
      ts = mktime(sprintf("%s %s %s %s %s %s", dt[1], dt[2], dt[3], dt[4], dt[5], dt[6]))
      if (ts >= cutoff) {
        msg = m2[1]
        gsub(/[^a-z0-9]/, "", tolower(msg))
        print "ERROR:" host "|" msg
      }
    }
  }
' | sort -u | cut -d: -f2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

This solution:
- Uses `find` with `-print0` to handle filenames with spaces
- Opens `.gz` files with `zcat` and regular logs with `cat`, skipping unreadable files
- Parses both text and JSON formats using `awk`
- Normalizes messages by lowercasing and stripping punctuation
- Filters entries within the last 8 hours using timestamp comparison
- Deduplicates per host using `sort -u`
